title: SHE WASN’T SUPPOSED TO TOUCH HIM.
paragraphs: SHE WASN’T SUPPOSED TO TOUCH HIM.

Twelve years of bleeding.
Twelve years of whispers.
Twelve years of being untouchable.

According to the law, she was unclean.
Anything she touched became unclean.
Anyone she touched became unclean.
So she learned to live in the shadows.

Back rows.
Covered face.
Silent shame.

Doctors took her money.
Hope drained from her body the same way the blood did.
And then she heard a name.
Jesus.
But here was the problem:

The crowd was thick.
And the Law said she shouldn’t touch anyone.
Yet something inside her refused to die.
Faith.

“If I just touch His garment… I will be healed.”
(Mark 5:28)

Not His hand.
Not His face.
Just the edge of His robe.
So she pushed through the crowd.

Every step risky.
Every shoulder brushed a violation.
Every heartbeat louder than the noise around her.
And then—
Her fingers touched the hem.
Instantly.

The bleeding stopped.
Strength returned.
Twelve years of suffering ended in a single second.
But Jesus stopped walking.
“Who touched My clothes?”

The disciples were confused.
The crowd was pressing everywhere.
But Jesus felt something different.
Power had moved.
And the woman froze.

Fear gripped her chest.
If she spoke, the whole crowd would know her secret.
But grace was standing right in front of her.

So she fell at His feet…
and told the whole truth.
Not just about the touch.

About the pain.
The isolation.
The shame.
And Jesus did not rebuke her.
He did not step back.
He did not call her unclean.
He called her something no one had called her in twelve years.
“Daughter.”

“Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace and be healed of your affliction.”
— Mark 5:34
Do you see the Gospel here?
She thought she was stealing a miracle.
But Jesus turned it into a relationship.

Religion said:
“Stay away. You’re unclean.”

Jesus said:
“Come near. You’re family.”
This is what Christ does.

He is not afraid of your shame.
Not afraid of your past.
Not afraid of the thing you hide from the crowd.
You may feel like you’re only reaching for the edge of His robe…
But grace is already reaching for you.
And when Jesus speaks over your life, He doesn’t call you by your failure.
He calls you:

Daughter.
Son.
Redeemed.
Someone in the crowd today is still bleeding in silence.
And they need to know:
One touch of Jesus changes everything.
“We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.”
